title: Congress Seeks Over 100 UP Seats as Seat-Sharing Talks With SP Open in Delhi
excerpt: The two INDIA bloc allies began formal negotiations on Monday for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, with the SP insisting that winnability, not seat counts, should drive the allocation.
body:
• Congress and the Samajwadi Party opened formal seat-sharing talks in New Delhi on Monday, November 23, for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.
  • According to sources, Congress is seeking more than 100 of the state's 403 seats, with a focus on about 55-60 constituencies it rates as its strongest.
  • SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav said after the first round that an agreement could be finalised within two to three days; talks resume on Tuesday.
  • No seat-sharing formula has been announced, and any arrangement still needs approval from both parties' leaderships.

The Congress and the Samajwadi Party (SP) began formal seat-sharing negotiations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in New Delhi on Monday, November 23, with senior SP leader Ram Gopal Yadav expressing confidence afterwards that an agreement could be finalised within the next two to three days. The first round of talks was held at the residence of Congress MP Pramod Tiwari, and discussions are set to resume on Tuesday.

Speaking after the meeting, Ram Gopal Yadav said both parties had presented their respective positions and listened to each other's views, and that the process was moving forward through mutual consultation, according to ITDC India's report of the talks. The Congress delegation at the meeting included Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, state president Aradhana Mishra, working state president Imran Masood and legislative party leader Virendra Chaudhary. The SP team comprised Ram Gopal Yadav, state president Shyamlal Pal and MPs Rajiv Rai and Iqra Hasan.

What Congress is asking for

According to sources cited in reporting on the negotiations, Congress is seeking more than 100 seats, including approximately 55-60 "A-grade" constituencies it considers favourable — seats where it secured a lead or lost narrowly in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, or where it has established local leaders. The party had earlier submitted a list of 181 Assembly constituencies to the SP, and it is drawing on the 2017 Assembly election arrangement, when the SP allotted it about 105 seats. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra is not expected to attend the meetings, although she is reportedly overseeing the negotiations from behind the scenes.

"We have made up our mind on how many seats we will contest, and the Samajwadi Party and the INDIA alliance will defeat the BJP together."

— Akhilesh Yadav, Samajwadi Party president, in PTI reporting

The SP's position: winnability first

The SP is emphasising candidate winnability rather than the overall number of seats allocated to its ally. According to sources, the SP has shared a list of around 55 constituencies with Congress, including several seats where the BJP is considered electorally strong. An SP MP reportedly argued that Congress secured only two Assembly seats and around 2 per cent of the vote in the 2022 Uttar Pradesh elections, and should therefore prioritise constituencies where it has performed relatively well and has a strong organisational presence.

Several constituencies could be contentious, particularly Saharanpur Dehat, Behat, Amethi and Rae Bareli — seats the SP won at the previous Assembly election but which Congress leaders have also expressed interest in contesting. Amethi and Rae Bareli carry particular significance for Congress because of their association with the Gandhi family, and the party's earlier list of 181 constituencies included all seats in those districts. One arrangement being discussed, according to the reporting, is for some SP leaders to contest on Congress tickets in constituencies where that could help the alliance.

What happens next

The two parties contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections together in Uttar Pradesh under the INDIA bloc. Their senior leaders, Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav, held preliminary discussions on November 16, according to the reports. Both sides are expected to examine constituency-level performance, previous election results and organisational presence before settling an allocation for the 403-member Assembly, where elections are scheduled for 2027. No final seat-sharing agreement had been announced as the talks opened, and the final arrangement will require approval from the respective party leaderships. The Indian Witness's account sets out each side's reported opening position in detail.
